sentences.text: This creature was a small, four-legged hunter on land that measured less than one meter in length.
Despite its tiny body size, its skull measured 9 cm, making it larger than other members of its group.
Unlike other crocodyliforms, it lacked specific holes in its lower jaw and in front of its eye sockets.
Paleontologists James Clark and George Callison first found its remains in 1975.
Before its official description in 2011, the animal was known only as the "Fruita form".
James Clark formally named it Fruitachampsa callisoni in 2011 to honor George Callison.
As a land-based predator, it possessed long and extremely slender limbs.
Its back was covered by two overlapping rows of bony plates called osteoderms, which were much thinner than those of modern crocodiles.
It is the only known shartegosuchid from North America and represents one of the youngest members of this group.
It lived during the Upper Jurassic period within the Morrison Formation of Colorado.
Its existence spanned between 152.21 and 143.1 million years ago, covering the Kimmeridgian to Tithonian stages.
Researchers suggest that the presence of Fruitachampsa indicates shartegosuchids migrated from Asia into North America via Europe during the Late Jurassic.
